title: LoRAStencil: Low-Rank Adaptation of Stencil Computation on Tensor Cores
problem: Stencil computations suffer from memory access redundancies and dimension residue on Tensor Core Units, limiting efficient execution. The paper identifies dimension residue as a nuanced form of TCU-specific redundancy that hinders performance.
motivation: Stencil computations are pivotal to scientific and industrial applications, but their efficient execution on specialized accelerators like Tensor Cores remains a significant challenge.
method: LoRAStencil speeds up stencil computations (repeatedly applying a pattern across a grid, common in physics simulations) on Tensor Cores—specialized matrix-processing hardware in GPUs—by decomposing weight patterns into low-rank components (simpler sub-matrices that combine to form the original). This simpler structure is easier to reorganize efficiently, so LoRAStencil uses three techniques: efficiently gathering misaligned data (Residual Dimension Gathering), organizing patterns hierarchically to match their structure (Pyramidal Matrix Adaptation), and using a butterfly algorithm for data rearrangement to avoid expensive shuffles (Butterfly Vector Swapping).
key_novelty: Decomposing stencil weight matrices into low-rank components to fix dimension residue (the performance loss when data dimensions don't align with Tensor Core hardware expectations) and enable efficient data gathering.
contributions: Identification and characterization of dimension residue as a TCU-specific form of memory redundancy
Low-rank adaptation technique to decompose stencil weight matrices into rank-1 components
Residual Dimension Gathering mechanism for memory-efficient data reuse
Butterfly Vector Swapping to circumvent all data shuffles in stencil computation
baselines: state-of-the-art stencil computing systems on tensor cores
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: low-rank stencil optimization on tensor cores
